_comment: Accepted deltas for the proto-audit netlink layout oracle.
The oracle (nix/checks/proto-audit-netlink.nix) compares xtcp2's Go netlink
structs against the Linux kernel UAPI headers and 14 other sources, indexed
by WIRE BIT OFFSET rather than by field name. Some reported deltas are
deliberate design choices, and some are limitations of proto-audit itself;
each one is recorded here so the check can gate without being permanently
red.
Reviewed like docs/coverage-baseline.txt: an entry is a standing decision,
so adding one needs the same scrutiny as lowering a coverage floor. A delta
that is merely inconvenient does not belong here — only one that is correct.
Keys are protocol names as proto-audit reports them (see `proto-audit list`).
Each entry is matched on protocol + offset_bits + field, so a field moving
to a different offset stops being allowlisted and the check goes red again.
That is intentional: the offset is the thing being asserted.
THREE KINDS APPEAR BELOW, and they are not equally permanent:
kind=semantic   proto-audit's own name-based type heuristic
(src/extractors/xtcp2.rs infer_field_type) labels a field
Enum/Flags where its kernel extractor says Uint. An
annotation disagreement, not a layout one. Permanent.
kind=split      one side models a C bitfield byte as a whole byte and the
other models the individual bitfields. Layout-equivalent.
Permanent until proto-audit's kernel extractor learns C
bitfields.
kind=upstream-registry-pin
NOT a real delta at all — proto-audit is reading the wrong
xtcp2 struct. DELETE these entries when the upstream fix
lands; see the note on NL_Diag_TCPInfo below.
_note_NL_Diag_TCPInfo: The 11 kind=upstream-registry-pin entries are a proto-audit bug, not an
xtcp2 gap, and this is worth stating precisely because it is the exact
opposite of what the oracle appears to say.
xdp2's protocol registry hardcodes the Go struct name:
samples/proto_audit/src/name_mapping/table.rs:552-555
PN::new("NL_Diag_TCPInfo", 248)
.kernel("tcp_info", "linux/tcp.h")
.xtcp2("TCPInfo6_10_3")
.variable(),
So the extractor is asked for TCPInfo6_10_3 — a 248-byte struct that ends at
tcpi_total_rto_time and predates Accurate ECN. Its resolve_alias() step
(src/extractors/xtcp2.rs:56) exists precisely to follow
`type TCPInfo TCPInfo7_0_3` to the newest variant, but it is never reached,
because the name it is handed is already a concrete struct rather than the
alias. Measured directly against THIS tree:
proto-audit extract --source xtcp2 --proto NL_Diag_TCPInfo --json
-> field_count 61, min_header_bytes 248
61 fields and 248 bytes is TCPInfo6_10_3 exactly. The AccECN trailer cannot
be reported as present because the struct being read does not contain it.
The offsets proto-audit reports for the 11 fields independently CONFIRM the
decoder rather than contradicting it. Its kernel extractor puts
tcpi_ecn_mode at bit 2208 = byte 276, with accecn_opt_seen at 2210,
accecn_fail_mode at 2212 and options2 at 2216 — i.e. one __u32 at [276:280]
split 2/2/4/24 in little-endian bit order. That is field-for-field what
pkg/xtcpnl/xtcpnl_inet_diag_tcpinfo.go:256-263 decodes.
Upstream fix is one word: `.xtcp2("TCPInfo")` instead of
`.xtcp2("TCPInfo6_10_3")`, letting resolve_alias() do its job. A second,
independent upstream nit found while diagnosing this: extract_size_const
(src/extractors/xtcp2.rs:143) builds the pattern `{struct}SizeCst`, but
xtcp2 spells these `TCPInfo7_0_3_SizeCst` with an underscore, so the size
constant is never found for any versioned variant and the size is inferred
from field offsets instead. Harmless here, but it means the `248` in the
registry is the only size proto-audit has.
Both are tracked in nix/upstream-pins.json; when the xdp2 pin is bumped past
a fix, these 11 entries must be deleted, at which point they should turn
into 11 agreements.

NL_Diag_TCPInfo.reason: proto-audit's infer_field_type() sees "state" in the name and labels xtcp2's field Enum; its kernel extractor says Uint. Both agree it is 8 bits at offset 0. Annotation, not layout.
Same heuristic as tcpi_state: "state" in the name yields Enum vs the kernel's Uint. Offset and size agree.

infer_field_type() labels anything containing "options" as Flags; the kernel extractor says Uint. It IS a flags byte (TCPI_OPT_TIMESTAMPS etc., linux/include/uapi/linux/tcp.h), so the heuristic is arguably the more accurate of the two. Offset and size agree.

Kernel byte 6 is `__u8 tcpi_snd_wscale:4, tcpi_rcv_wscale:4` (linux/include/uapi/linux/tcp.h). xtcp2 decodes the two nibbles into SndWscale and RcvWscale, which is the kernel's own view; proto-audit's kernel extractor does not model C bitfields and emits a single 8-bit field for the byte, so the nibbles read as overlapping it. Layout-equivalent.
The kernel-side half of the same disagreement: proto-audit emits the whole of byte 6 as one 8-bit field and reports it overlapping xtcp2's two nibbles. Same single root cause as tcpi_snd_wscale @48.
Low nibble of kernel byte 6; see tcpi_snd_wscale @48.

Kernel byte 7 is `__u8 tcpi_delivery_rate_app_limited:1, tcpi_fastopen_client_fail:2`. xtcp2 decodes the individual bits; proto-audit's kernel extractor emits byte 7 whole (as `rcv_wscale`, its name for it), so the bits read as overlapping. Layout-equivalent.

Kernel-side half of the byte-7 disagreement. The NAME is also off by one byte on proto-audit's side — rcv_wscale is really the low nibble of byte 6 — which is a symptom of the same missing bitfield support, and is why this allowlist matches on offset rather than on name.
Bits 1-2 of kernel byte 7; see tcpi_delivery_rate_app_limited @56.

A phantom: having spent a whole byte on each of the two byte-7 bitfields, proto-audit's kernel extractor lands this one on byte 8, which is really tcpi_rto — hence `overlaps with: tcpi_rto`. xtcp2's Rto @64 is correct and is confirmed by the pcap corpus (validate-netlink grades NL_Diag_TCPInfo Gold across 8 kernel versions). Downstream of the same missing bitfield support.
Second phantom byte from the same cause; see delivery_rate_app_limited @64.
Reported missing because proto-audit reads TCPInfo6_10_3, not TCPInfo7_0_3. Present at pkg/xtcpnl/xtcpnl_inet_diag_tcpinfo.go:248, byte [248:252]. See _note_NL_Diag_TCPInfo.
Present at xtcpnl_inet_diag_tcpinfo.go:249, byte [252:256]. See _note_NL_Diag_TCPInfo.
Present at xtcpnl_inet_diag_tcpinfo.go:250, byte [256:260]. See _note_NL_Diag_TCPInfo.
Present at xtcpnl_inet_diag_tcpinfo.go:251, byte [260:264]. See _note_NL_Diag_TCPInfo.
Present at xtcpnl_inet_diag_tcpinfo.go:252, byte [264:268]. See _note_NL_Diag_TCPInfo.

Present at xtcpnl_inet_diag_tcpinfo.go:253, byte [268:272]. Independently corroborated on the wire: in two of the three 7.0.3 fixtures this field equals tcpi_bytes_received exactly (11648 and 98264), which is what RFC3168-mode ECN (tcpi_ecn_mode=1) should produce. See _note_NL_Diag_TCPInfo.
Present at xtcpnl_inet_diag_tcpinfo.go:254, byte [272:276]. See _note_NL_Diag_TCPInfo.
Present at xtcpnl_inet_diag_tcpinfo.go:260 as bits 0-1 of the __u32 at [276:280] — the same bit offset proto-audit's kernel extractor reports. See _note_NL_Diag_TCPInfo.
Present at xtcpnl_inet_diag_tcpinfo.go:261 as bits 2-3 of the [276:280] __u32. See _note_NL_Diag_TCPInfo.
Present at xtcpnl_inet_diag_tcpinfo.go:262 as bits 4-7 of the [276:280] __u32. See _note_NL_Diag_TCPInfo.
